newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal to complete key local polls.
newsitem.headline: Nepal to complete key local polls.

text.p: Nepal on Monday holds the second and last phase of local polls which the main communist party said would increase pressure for a mid-term general election.
Voters in 35 districts will choose new village development committees and municipal authorities, which are the Himalayan kingdom's equivalent of local councils.

Initial results from the first phase, held on May 17, showed the communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party was well ahead of both its ruling coalition partner, the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), and the opposition Nepali Congress.
The Election Commission said out of 44,500 seats decided, the UML had won 21,700 and Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand's RPP had taken 5,500.
Nepali Congress, which had won control of most of the local bodies in elections held in 1992, had taken 13,800 so far.
In all, about 190,000 representatives will be elected in 4,000 village committees and 58 municipalities for a five-year term.
Local bodies plan and oversee village level development activities in the mountainous nation, one of the 10 poorest countries of the world.
The outcome of the local elections was not likely to have a direct impact on the government in Kathmandu, where Chand is leading a tenuous two-month-old coalition with the UML.
But communists said the results could increase pressure on Chand to call snap elections to the national parliament.
"The composition of the present parliament cannot solve the problem of the country. Therefore, a mid-term election is necessary," said UML central committee member Pradeep Nepal.

The last general election in November 1994 yielded a deeply split lower house of parliament. The UML controls 90 seats, Congress 87 and the RPP 20 in the 205-member House of Representatives, whose term would normally run until 1999.
Chand has said snap polls were not part of the 20-point agreement he reached with the UML in cobbling together the coalition.
